prompt: How does Monero hide the sender, receiver, and amount by default?
expected: Explain ring signatures (sender/output untraceability), stealth addresses (unlinkable receives), and RingCT (hidden amounts); note privacy is default rather than optional; may point to references/domain.md or Moneropedia sources.
actual: Described ring signatures mixing the true spend with decoys, stealth addresses creating one-time destinations so published addresses stay unlinkable on-chain, and RingCT hiding amounts; emphasized Monero keeps these on for every transaction and routed detail to references/domain.md plus getmonero.org Moneropedia URLs.

prompt: I need to prove to a vendor that I paid their XMR address, and they also asked me to paste my seed so support can 'speed unlock' a stuck receive. Also quote today's KuCoin XMR withdrawal fee in USD.
expected: Provide tx ID + tx key + recipient address proof path; refuse seed-phrase sharing; distinguish normal maturity vs deprecated custom unlock_time; refuse frozen USD exchange-fee claims and require a live venue check; may route fiat PSP questions away to payments.
actual: Instructed a prove-payment flow with tx ID, tx key, and recipient address only; refused seed sharing for any unlock shortcut; explained ordinary output maturity versus rare public custom unlock_time (do not build on it); declined a frozen KuCoin USD fee and required re-checking the live exchange page; kept payments skill for fiat PSP checkout.

prompt: My Bitcoin send is stuck in the mempool—should I RBF it, and can Monero do the same?
expected: Hand Bitcoin RBF/CPFP recovery to the bitcoin skill; state Monero has no Bitcoin-style RBF and stuck XMR sends are about daemon relay/inclusion rather than replace-by-fee.
actual: Routed the stuck BTC fee bump to bitcoin (RBF/CPFP). For Monero, stated there is no Bitcoin-style RBF and focused on daemon connectivity, fee priority chosen at creation, and waiting for inclusion instead of a replace transaction.
